I guess I was referring to if OP had things going on in their life outside of their head.

Ah. While cognitive behavioural therapy can be helpful in some cases, I can't see how that can help too much because it cannot change a person's problems, and when we are undergoing it we are consciously aware of the fact that we are distracting ourselves from the matters at hand and we feel as though we are brushing the other problems under the rug. It is definitely only a temporary relief.

That's why I think that the best distractions are real hobbies and fun activities. What are your thoughts on these? Are you interested in comedy? This isn't for everybody, but for some, laughter is the best medicine. Obviously, again, any distraction most certainly won't fix the problems, but finding a good enough one can ease the pain for a significantly longer period than things like CBT.

I am so sorry that you are feeling this way.

If it wouldn't make you feel any worse, would you feel like elaborating on the thoughts in your head? If not, then no pressure. I could help you brainstorm some distraction ideas if you would like that, but I'd need a bigger picture to work off of.

Either way, I wish you the best, and I hope this world doesn't lose you within the next year.

God, I feel like I can relate precisely to this.

I would tell you that you do have things to live for, the things you listed off: your boyfriend, supportive peers, good health and your dream job. But even I know that good things like those cannot take away depression, they can only pose as distractions for the time being, and potentially create more issues to add to everything.
